test_title: PYST 56: SSC MTS 2024 - General Awareness (Held On: 11 Nov, 2024 - Shift 3)
subject: gk
question:
Which of the following is an example of a physical change? In this example, there is no change in chemical composition of matter.

A: Coal changing into coal ash on burning

B: Preparing a sweet drink by mixing sugar in water

C: White washing walls using a solution of lime and water

D: Mixing salt and lemon juice in a beaker
solution:
The correct answer is __**4 - Only B: Preparing a sweet drink by mixing sugar in water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Physical Change:** A physical change is a type of change in which the form of matter is altered, but its chemical composition remains unchanged.
 
• **Dissolving sugar in water** is a physical change because the sugar molecules disperse in the water without forming a new substance.
 
• The process is reversible; the sugar can be retrieved by evaporating the water, leaving the chemical composition of the sugar intact.
 
• In this example, no chemical bonds are broken or formed, and the sugar retains its chemical identity.
 
• Other examples of physical changes include melting, freezing, condensation, and breaking a material into smaller pieces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chemical Change:** A chemical change involves a transformation where the chemical composition of a substance changes, resulting in the formation of new substances.
 
• **Example of Chemical Change:** Burning coal to form coal ash is a chemical change because the carbon in coal reacts with oxygen, producing carbon dioxide and ash, substances with different chemical compositions.
 
• **Reversibility:** Physical changes are generally reversible, while chemical changes are often irreversible under normal conditions.
 
• **Indicators of Chemical Changes:** Common indicators include the emission of gas, change in temperature, formation of a precipitate, or a change in color.
 
• **Whitewashing:** In whitewashing (lime and water), slaked lime reacts chemically with carbon dioxide in the air to form calcium carbonate, a chemical change.
